about: what gw's tests expect of GW150914-v3.json, GWOSC's event api json for GW150914, fetched 2026-10-30 from https://gwosc.org/eventapi/json/event/GW150914/v3 (sha256 1ce014e3277cc6ef491daa48250465eefda026f2b974d2a15bb8c6ea5596e37e), 13,903 bytes. its licence is recalled as cc by 4.0, the open science centre's, and not read. each value is as that file gives it, in GWOSC's units; the tests turn celestial's si back into those units to compare. the utc time is that file's gps 1126259462.4 as utc, 09:50:45.4 on 2015-09-14; LIGO's discovery paper (Abbott et al. 2016, PRL 116, 061102, read 2026-10-31 from arXiv:1602.03837) gives 09:50:45 utc, to the second, so the tenth is gwosc's, not the paper's

drawn about: picked for the property, 2026-10-31: values from 10^-10 to 10^10 of the centre's unit, written over the file's own for a mass or a distance, and units of one to eight small letters, which the centre's table has none of
units about: each unit the centre writes, in si, typed from its definition and not worked out by celestial's measure: a solar mass as the iau's nominal 1.98841e30 kg, measure's own test's figure, to a part in a million; a megaparsec as a million parsecs of 648000/pi au of 149597870700 m, the iau's definitions; a solar mass times c squared as 1.98841e30 kg times 299792458 m/s squared, multiplied out by hand; and a square degree as (pi/180)^2 steradians. each parameter is one the file gives in that unit, at the value the file gives
